notes: Both coders found the same single document (UMSL CTL sample statements) and agreed on stance (delegates) and on most units. Main disagreements: (1) phase for rationale and own-work passages (course-start or during-work vs general), settled by whether the passage states a rule applied during work or a principle; (2) type for bans (P01 vs P19 vs P05 vs P29), settled by what the sentence actually bans; (3) P24 vs P28 for the Level 5 no-disclosure sentence (P24 with fit note); (4) P15 vs P16 for the UMass brainstorm/draft sentence (P15 because P16 is about code); (5) modality for the tech-free writing and 'permitted/encouraged' sentences; (6) unit_stance, mostly neutral vs restrict/require for penalty and citation duties; (7) A merged the assignment-instructions commitment with the scale sentence while B coded it as its own P09 unit (kept). Seven A-only units were kept (graduated penalties, follow the AI scale, evaluate AI output, contravene integrity rules, IP/misinformation duty, learning-goal rationale, shared responsibility) and five dropped (purpose-of-guidance clause, reflection purpose clause, Perkins credit line, Temple lead-in sentence, false-quotations unit folded into the no-credit unit). Group work (A UNCOVERED, B P19) resolved to P19 with A's note kept in fit_note.
